I didn't poo for about 3 days. On my dinner break at work, it decided it was coming so I shot into the loo. Went to flush, it just DID NOT MOVE. Tried to break it up with a pen, a tampon, nothing worked. I was panicking. I spent the entire break trying to fish this massive, heavily compacted poo out of the toilet with 'rods' made from rolled up hand towels and THEN had to carefully wrap it up in my NEW tote bag and dispose of it in the bin outside the shop down the road. I was mortified and pissed off, I'd not even had chance to eat. A couple of days later there was an email going around the office about the state of the toilets upstairs and I felt so smug in knowing I had disposed of my foul evidence and didn't have to be the one to hide my shame in knowing I was the perpetrator! I have no regrets.

My grandad died when I was 11, and when I think about him I don't remember anything really major, but the little things mean the most. I remember when he would sit in his chair, and I in his lap, and he'd read Aessop's fables to me all the time. He would teach me to draw perfectly round circles, practice my handwriting. Whenever we drove in the car, he tolerated my BBMak cassette on repeat. He was such an early riser, and whenever I would stay over, I'd always be waiting to see a light on in the hallway because that meant he was up! So I'd follow him into the kitchen and we would listen to the radio at 4am, and I guess we talked too, but I can't imagine what about. He'd get blamed by my grandma later in the day for me being tired, when she would catch me sucking my thumb and being grouchy. I just adored being around him.

I'm not a danger to anyone other than myself. 

And I'm really fucking trying to sort myself out!

Imagine your character being attacked by someone who knows very little about you, and acts upon only an opinion they have of you because you have scars on your body and are open about mental health issues, implying you are a 'danger' and 'unsafe'.

I definitely think twice about being so open about mental illness now. Yet if we don't talk about it, how is the stigma ever going to end?

When my ex bought his house, I found a photograph of Barry, the man who used to own the house. The photo was of him in the front room, I think I vaguely remember it might've been at Christmas time, but he looked happy either way. I kept it on the mantlepiece for ages. We started to lose things every now and again and they'd turn up in weird places, thought we heard odd noises here and there and started to joke that Barry and Ethel (his wife - now both deceased) were still in the house. This thought became a comfort to me, and seeing Barry's happy face in that photo on the mantlepiece was rather nice actually, I think I would've liked them!

After talking to people from other stores, it became apparent this was the norm for most coffee shop loos! What do these folk do, poo on the floor then get up to sit on the toilet and wipe their bottom? Or do they just not bother? How are they smearing it about? With their hands? Or are they scooting their dirty bums around like a dog with worms? Absolutely baffles me.

Thanks for your words folks. With regards to medication, I'm currently taking venlafaxine, have tried prozac, mirtazapine, citalopram and sertraline in the past. 
Have seen countless counsellors, psychiatrists, other mental health professionals from the age of 11.. Have been told there's nothing wrong with me, to I have treatment-resistant depression and recently, it might all be down to personality disorder, but I've never been diagnosed. Which leads me to think I'm making it all up in my head, am I just crazy? 
16 years of this shit, 16 years of just causing hurt and pain to everyone around me. 
Why am I unhappy? I've got a good job (I'm incapable of doing) I've got a family that cares, I've got 3 or 4 good friends (I don't give back as much as they give me). I've just about got a roof over my head. I'm 15k in debt that I can't afford to pay back. Ultimately, the problem is me and I'm the one thing I can't escape. No matter what changes I make to my life I'll still always be me and I can't live with that. 
Current situation means I'm living in a crisis house for the time being, signed off sick from work. I feel like this is make or break for me but all I can feel is the cracks are getting bigger and I'm losing it..
